title: COTS 2+ Mission
description:
On Tuesday, May 22 at 3:44 a.m. ET, Falcon 9 launched Dragon’s second demonstration mission under NASA’s Commercial Orbital Transportation Services program (COTS 2+) to the International Space Station from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. Approximately three days later on Friday, May 25, the Dragon spacecraft was captured and then berthed to the space station at 12:02 a.m. ET.

After five days, Dragon was released from the orbiting laboratory at 5:49 a.m. ET on Thursday, May 31 and successfully returned to Earth, splashing down off the coast of Baja, California at 8:42 a.m. PT. This was SpaceX’s second Commercial Orbital Transportation Services mission (COTS 2+) for NASA and the first time in history a private spacecraft visited the space station.

title: COTS 1 Mission
description:
On Wednesday, December 8 at 10:43 a.m. ET, Falcon 9 launched Dragon’s first demonstration mission under NASA’s Commercial Orbital Transportation Services program (COTS 1) to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida.

SpaceX’s Dragon spacecraft separated from Falcon 9 just over nine minutes into flight and achieved a nominal orbit. The spacecraft successfully returned to Earth and splashed down off the coast of Baja, California less than four hours later at 11:02 a.m. PT.

title: Falcon 9 Demo Mission
description:
On Friday, June 4 at 2:45 p.m. ET, Falcon 9 launched the Falcon 9 Demo mission to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 40 (SLC-40) at Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida.

This was the first flight for the Falcon 9 program.

title: RazakSAT Mission
description:
On Tuesday, July 14 at 3:35 p.m. MHT, Falcon 1 launched the  RazakSAT mission to low-Earth orbit from the SpaceX launch site on Omelek Island in the Marshall Islands.

This was the final flight in the Falcon 1 program.

title: RatSat Mission
description:
On Monday, September 29 at 11:15 a.m. MHT, Falcon 1 launched the  RatSat  mission to low-Earth orbit from the SpaceX launch site on Omelek Island in the Marshall Islands.

This was Falcon 1’s first successful mission and the first privately developed liquid fuel rocket to reach low-Earth orbit.

title: Trailblazer Mission
description:
On Sunday, August 3 at 3:34 p.m. MHT, Falcon 1 attempted to launch the Trailblazer mission to low-Earth orbit from the SpaceX launch site on Omelek Island in the Marshall Islands.

This was the first and final flight of the Falcon 1 booster supporting this mission.

title: DemoSat Mission
description:
On Wednesday, March 21 at 1:10 p.m. MHT, Falcon 1 attempted to launch the DemoSat mission to low-Earth orbit from the SpaceX launch site on Omelek Island in the Marshall Islands.

This was the first and final flight of the Falcon 1 booster supporting this mission.

title: FalconSAT-2 Mission
description:
On Friday, March 24 at 7:00 p.m. MHT, Falcon 1 attempted to launch the FalconSAT-2 mission to low-Earth orbit from the SpaceX launch site on Omelek Island in the Marshall Islands.

This was the first and final flight of the Falcon 1 booster supporting this mission.

title: Starlink Mission
description:
SpaceX’s Falcon 9 is targeting the launch of 24 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit from Space Launch Complex 4 East (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

A live webcast of this mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX.

This will be the 14th flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched SDA T1TL-B, SDA T1TL-C, Transporter-16, and 10 Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on the Of Course I Still Love You droneship, which will be stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

There is the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experience will depend on weather and other conditions.

title: NROL-179 Mission
description:
SpaceX is targeting Thursday, June 18 for a Falcon 9 launch of the NROL-179 mission from Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E) at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. The 35-minute launch window opens at 1:54 a.m. PT with a backup opportunity available at 1:40 a.m. PT on Friday, June 19.

A live webcast of the NROL-179 mission will begin about 10 minutes prior to liftoff, which you can watch here and on X @SpaceX.

This will be the third flight for the first stage booster supporting this mission, which previously launched two Starlink missions. Following stage separation, the first stage will land on Landing Zone 4 (LZ-4) at Vandenberg Space Force Base.

There is the possibility that residents of Santa Barbara, San Luis Obispo, and Ventura counties may hear  one or more sonic booms during the launch, but what residents experience will depend on weather and other conditions.
